observed_body:
Closes #277

## Summary

One user intent creates at most one transfer. A canonical payload fingerprint is bound to an idempotency key; only a safe operation reference is persisted across navigation/refresh; an edited payload requires a new intent.

## Design

- **`fingerprintTransferPayload` / `idempotencyKeyFor`** (`src/utils/transferIntent.js`) derive a stable key from the exact transferable fields (recipient, currencies, amounts, fee, rate).
- **Safe operation reference** in `sessionStorage`: key, fingerprint, transfer id, and operation status (`submitting` | `unknown` | `succeeded` | `failed` | `dismissed`). No secrets or raw form state.
- **`createTransfer`** returns the prior record for the same idempotency key, including concurrent in-flight replays (timeout / double-submit race).
- **Send Money** restores recoverable intents after navigation/refresh without auto-resubmitting. Dismissing the success dialog marks the op acknowledged. Timeout / connection-loss paths keep status `unknown` so a retry reuses the same key.
- **Changed payload** → new fingerprint → new idempotency key → new intent.

## Tradeoffs

- Session-scoped persistence (not cross-tab durable storage) keeps the reference safe and short-lived; a full backend idempotency store remains the long-term authority.
- Fee/rate are part of the fingerprint so a materially different quote is a new intent; cosmetic form edits that do not change the committed quote do not mint extras.
- Additive Transfer contract field `idempotencyKey` (optional) preserves legacy records.

## Compatibility

- Additive only; existing flows and the in-memory submission lock remain.
- Unrelated tests only gained `sessionStorage.clear()` in `beforeEach` so intent refs cannot leak across suites.

## Test evidence

```text
npx vitest run \
  test/unit/transfer-intent.test.js \
  test/unit/create-transfer-idempotency.test.js \
  test/integration/send-money-idempotency.test.jsx
# Test Files  3 passed | Tests  13 passed
npm run build  # ok
```

Coverage includes double-confirm, refresh restore, timeout key reuse, navigation reconcile, and changed-payload new key. Pre-existing failures on `main` (e.g. quote decimal formatting assertions) are untouched.

## Out of scope

- Broad rewrites, unrelated services, or cosmetic-only changes.
prior_prepared_body:
Closes #277

## Summary

One user intent creates at most one transfer. A canonical payload fingerprint is bound to an idempotency key, a safe operation reference survives navigation and refresh, and changed transfer details require a new intent. Confirmation now also requires a completed wallet connection and sufficient balance before saving an operation or creating a transfer.

## Changes

- Bind the canonical recipient, currencies, amounts, fee, and rate to an intent key. Persist only the key, opaque fingerprint, transfer ID, and operation status in sessionStorage.
- Return the existing transfer for repeated uses of the same key, including concurrent in-flight replays. Restore recoverable status after navigation or refresh without automatically resubmitting.
- Preserve unknown status after timeout or connection loss so an explicit retry can reuse the original key. Changed payloads create a new intent; dismissing a completed result acknowledges that operation.
- Require a readable object-map recovery journal and a successful submitting-reference save before addTransfer. A pre-submit storage failure refuses the transfer without replacing existing bytes and keeps the in-memory key available for retry. The demonstration API separately requires its local record to persist before acknowledging creation; late status-save failures cannot hide an already accepted transfer.
- Require the actual wallet returned by connect(). Rejected or incomplete connections and insufficient newly connected balances stop before fingerprint generation, journal mutation, or createTransfer. Canonical balance comparison preserves exact fractional balances.
- Keep the existing SubtleCrypto SHA-256 representation when SubtleCrypto is unavailable by lazily using the already-installed Stellar SDK hash implementation. The old 32-bit fallback could bind different payloads to the same recovery fingerprint.
- Refuse automatic rebinding or a new intent while an unresolved legacy weak fingerprint needs reconciliation. Preserve its original key and stored bytes; accepted legacy transfers still reconcile through the existing history.
- Report a pricing failure when a validated amount cannot be quoted. The maintained offline, form, precision, and quote cases now follow the actual confirmation/result flow and canonical decimal contract.

## Compatibility and tradeoffs

The optional Transfer idempotencyKey field preserves legacy records. Session-scoped persistence is not cross-tab durable storage; a live backend remains the authority for production idempotency. Fee and rate are part of the fingerprint, so a materially different quote is a new intent. The existing submission lock remains.

Package, lockfile, scripts, test configuration, formatter configuration, and ignore rules are unchanged. The required formatter was applied to its thirteen flagged files. No cases were removed, skipped, or added by the final acceptance pass.

## Current validation

Current source: [7640c5fd](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/commit/7640c5fdce9cb14bf6bf715bc6897d48d8da0b43).

- Complete maintained package selection: **522 passed across 51 files**, 65.64 seconds, Node 24.19.0 and Vitest 4.1.10, two workers.
- Existing Prettier check: passed.
- npm audit --audit-level=critical: exit 0, zero critical findings; 20 high, 12 moderate, and 2 low findings remain.
- Vite 5.4.21 production build: passed in 4.79 seconds, 122 modules.
- Exact command, composition details, and the separate earlier hosted result: [validation record](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/7640c5fdce9cb14bf6bf715bc6897d48d8da0b43/docs/validation/crypto-recovery.md).

Coverage includes double-confirm, refresh, timeout key reuse, navigation reconciliation, changed payloads, rejected/incomplete wallet connection, new-wallet balance checks, unchanged unknown-operation bytes followed by same-key retry, fallback hash equivalence, and legacy recovery. The earlier isolated hosted crypto run remains recorded as 9 passed / 1 failed; its warning-prefix assertion was corrected before the combined passing local run.

## Earlier browser execution

The retained built-App execution at [91ccb2cb](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/commit/91ccb2cb1071cae139f9be2d503395cb888d9f86) passed 23 browser checks. It reproduced duplicate local-demo records across reload when journal writes failed on the parent, then verified refusal, same-key recovery, and restoration with the repair. [Desktop and phone captures](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/91ccb2cb1071cae139f9be2d503395cb888d9f86/README.md#transfer-recovery-storage) retain that source-specific result; it was not rerun for the current continuation.

## Validation boundary

Mounted-app execution uses the repository's demonstration wallet and transfer service. Live provider idempotency, settlement, and cross-tab persistence are outside this result. The deferred SDK fallback chunk is 903.71 kB minified / 234.96 kB gzip and retains the build's size warning.

The upstream Node 22 [CI](https://github.com/RemitFlow/RemitFlow-Frontend/actions/runs/37195231027) and [Lighthouse CI](https://github.com/RemitFlow/RemitFlow-Frontend/actions/runs/37195231019) runs report action_required; the local result is separate from hosted acceptance.
